messages:
alex_infra: heads up — asia-east1 GPU pool reporting high RTs and ~40% pod evictions, customers seeing 503s. we kicked off autoscale but traffic still piling on old endpoints. suspect DNS failover/propagation lag.
maria_sre: on it. can you paste the runbook step you tried? did you change GSLB weights or DNS TTLs?
todd_ops: i changed GSLB weight to steer 80% -> us-west and 20% -> eu-central at 1719003200, then set authoritative TTL to 30s. i also triggered cache-bust on the gslb service.
dns-monitor: alert: authoritative record updated (asia.redwood.example) TTL=30 at 1719003220. however resolver graphs show many upstream resolvers still returning 300s for that FQDN.
alex_infra: ugh — so TTLs didn't clamp down for a bunch of clients. dig from a handful of vantage points:

```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> asia.redwood.example @ns1.redwood.example
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 54321
;; ANSWER SECTION:
asia.redwood.example. 300 IN A 35.200.1.22
```

that 300 is the cached value from some ISP resolvers despite our authoritative change.
maria_sre: this looks like resolver-side clamp/caching. some resolvers ignore lowered TTLs for DDoS/caching policy. next steps: 1) GSLB weight cut to 0 for asia-east1 2) announce manual BGP steering for critical prefixes 3) spin up minimal on-demand GPUs in ap-south1 as buffer. thoughts?
liu_oncall: confirmed — a subset of dig probes still show old IPs. @todd_ops did we also update any CNAME aliases? some services use short CNAME chains, that can extend effective TTL.
todd_ops: good catch — there's a legacy cname: gpu.api.redwood -> asia.redwood.example. i updated both but some downstream resolvers may have cached the cname chain. i've opened ticket with our CDN partner to request an emergency cache purge for that cname.
jess_platform: if DNS purge will take unknown time, we should accept partial traffic in asia but degrade workload: switch model->quantized-small fallback for that region to lower GPU needs. that buys time and avoids full failover cost.
sam_cost: FYI: spinning up on-demand capacity in ap-south1 for the short term estimated at ~$12k/day. fallback model reduces cost a lot (approx 65% token cost reduction). choose tradeoff.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered by @jess_platform: rollout quantized-small to asia-east1 as canary (5% traffic) at 1719003300. status: in_progress.
alex_infra: action list so far: gslb weight -> 0 for asia-east1 (todd), request CDN purge (todd), BGP announce for critical prefixes (maria), spin on-demand in ap-south1 (jess + infra), canary quantized fallback (deploy-bot). prioritize: BGP + GSLB weight first to reduce new sessions hitting asia.
maria_sre: doing BGP prep now. note: BGP will not affect clients that have cached A records, only new flows. combine with a graceful drain of gpu pool (cordon nodes) to allow existing sessions to finish.
liu_oncall: cordoning nodes now. `kubectl cordon gpu-pool-asia-*` then set pod eviction grace to 60s. starting at 1719003350.
alex_infra: observed initial drop in error rate after weight change + cordon. but still ~5% of traffic to asia due to cached resolvers. those are low-volume but high-latency; will keep an eye.
dns-monitor: note: a subset of major ISP resolvers in APAC are clamping TTLs to 300-600s for stability. Ops runbook update suggestion: when doing critical failover, prefer immediate GSLB weight + BGP + app-level fallbacks rather than relying on low authoritative TTL alone.
maria_sre: agreed. i'm documenting: "DNS alone is insufficient for immediate failover due to resolver clamps — always plan for BGP/GSLB + model fallback." adding to post-incident checklist.
alex_infra: timeline: incident opened 1719003333, initial GSLB weight change 1719003200 (pre-thread), authoritative TTL -> 30 at 1719003220, BGP announce 1719003360, node cordon 1719003350, quantized canary 1719003300. last observed 503s dropped below baseline at 1719003410.
sam_cost: recommend follow-up: estimate cost delta and propose temporary budget approval for ap-south1 on-demand run for 48h. i'll draft a slack thread for finance after this.
jess_platform: post-incident tasks: revert quantized fallback when asia stabilizes, reflow traffic slowly, add explicit cname TTLs to the DNS playbook, and run tabletop for resolver-clamp scenarios.
alex_infra: thanks everyone. closing primary incident channel when last_message_ts passes 1719003421. we'll capture the runbook edits in a PR. :white_check_mark:
